Title: Reimagining Education for Girls
NewsSummary: Nooreen Aziz, a trailblazer from Sindh, is determined to make a difference in her community
NewsContent:
Growing up in Mulko Wahan, a small village near Ranipur Sugar Mills in Khairpur District, Sindh, Nooreen Aziz felt the weight of inequality. It was clear to her from an early age that something had to change. She remembers sitting in class, watching the boys eagerly raise their hands while she was told to wait her turn. 

In her village, nearly half (49.7%) of females are literate, compared to 72.9% of males. This sense of disparity stayed with Nooreen, fueling her drive to change the narrative for future generations, and leading her to pursue a Master of Philosophy (MPhil) in Education at AKU-IED.

At AKU-IED, Nooreen found herself in a new role-training teachers at Oriental Grammar School. She introduced technology into their lesson plans, and the impact was immediate. Teachers were enthusiastic, realizing that these tools could transform their classrooms into dynamic, interactive spaces that fostered real student engagement. They couldn't wait for the next training session. 

Nooreen also led a workshop called Transforming Teaching and Learning, where she taught teachers how to use digital tools like Padlet and Google Docs to enhance student engagement and foster collaborative learning environments. The feedback was overwhelmingly positive, with many teachers eager to incorporate these tools into their own teaching practices.

One of Nooreen's most meaningful contributions was her involvement in the development of the Single National Curriculum Computer Science Assessment Framework for grades VI-VIII. She played a pivotal role in shaping the framework by emphasizing project-based assessments that encourage critical thinking and digital literacy. "My work was part of a larger initiative to equip students with not just knowledge, but the skills they need to succeed in an increasingly digital world," she explains.

Additionally, as a member of the Arts & Culture Committee at AKU-IED, Nooreen helped organize the Spring Festival, a vibrant celebration of diverse cultural traditions. The event, which honoured occasions like Navroz, Pakistan Day, Holi, and Easter, embodied the unity and inclusivity Noreen values so deeply.

Nooreen's time at AKU-IED has strengthened her vision for a brighter future. "Today, I continue to work towards accessible education, women's empowerment, and sustainable community growth, proudly carrying forward AKU's mission to create a lasting impact."

As an educationist and entrepreneur, Nooreen is ready to return to her roots, her heart set on one goal: bringing the opportunity and knowledge she's gained back to her community. 

"I aim to establish a non-formal education setup in my village, providing flexible learning opportunities for both children and adults," she says with conviction. By creating a peer-to-peer network of trained women and collaborating with organizations like the Teach the World Foundation, Nooreen hopes to scale sustainable educational solutions that blend traditional values with modern tools.
